findings_qualitative.value: HNC (4-3) absorption between 7.15 and 7.60 km/s traces an extended redshifted foreground layer covering both sources

evidence.quote: our HNC (4$-$3) results confirm the existence of a previously inferred redshifted foreground layer.

findings_qualitative.value: Both outflows are well collimated along N-S; 4A2 outflow is S-shaped

evidence.quote: 4A1 and 4A2 each display a well-collimated outflow along the N-S direction, and an S-shaped morphology can be discerned in the outflow powered by 4A2.

claims.hypothesis: Infall parameters from low-resolution single-dish models extrapolate to the 4A1 inner envelope
claims.experiment: SPARX RT models with mock ALMA observations compared with observed H2CO spectra
claims.result: Observed profiles are Gaussian absorption with ~1 km/s widths and no infall >~0.5 km/s, unlike the models
claims.finding: Parameters cannot be directly extrapolated; infall at 75 au at least 8x slower; rate at most ~3e-5 Msun/yr

evidence.quote: we estimate the radial inward motion at a radius of 75 au should be at least a factor of 8 slower than that extrapolated from the velocity structure deduced by (cite: mot13).

claims.experiment: Examined H2CO spectra and absorption opacity vs velocity
claims.result: Absorbing dips are skewed redward, narrow, up to ~8 km/s
claims.finding: Likely infall of 0.4-0.8 km/s, rate 3.1-6.2e-5 Msun/yr at 100 au

evidence.quote: the absorbing dips in the H$_2$CO spectra are indeed skewed toward the red-shifted side and likely signatures of inward motion.

claims.hypothesis: A foreground absorbing layer exists toward IRAS 4A
claims.result: Extended HNC absorption at 7.15-7.60 km/s with no velocity gradient, absent in H2CO
claims.finding: HNC traces a redshifted foreground layer

evidence.quote: we favor the HNC (4$-$3) absorption observed between 7.15 km s$^{-1}$ and 7.60 km s$^{-1}$ tracing an extended redshifted foreground layer

why_this_method.value: Absorption against continuum (inverse P-Cygni) is a robust probe of infall, and ALMA gives high resolution

evidence.quote: The “inverse P-Cygni” line profile, i.e., the redshifted self-absorption of spectral lines, is considered as a more robust probe of infall motions.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Disk-face-on hot corino atmosphere (Scenario I) vs temperature-stratified envelope (Scenario II) for 4A1 absorption; undecided

evidence.quote: High-resolution observations of disk tracers at low frequency may help to discriminate the two scenarios

limitations_admitted.value: 1D collapse model likely breaks down; no full RT modelling for 4A2 possible due to complex structure

evidence.quote: The lack of a proper description for the complex mixture of disk, outflow, and envelope components around 4A2 prevents us from formulating a full RT modeling experiment.
